definition: Recognizing signs from sign-language video — isolated sign classification or continuous signing — distinct from full sign-language translation.
details: Recognizing signs from sign-language video — isolated sign classification or continuous signing — distinct from full sign-language translation.

explainer.lead: Sign language recognition is the task of recognizing signs from sign-language video, either as isolated sign classification or continuous signing. It matters as a component distinct from full sign-language translation.

tiers.eli5: It is the computer picking out individual signs from a video of someone signing, not yet turning the whole thing into spoken words.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers build it as isolated sign classification or continuous signing recognition. A pitfall is conflating recognition with translation, which is a separate task.
tiers.paperLevel: Formally, sign language recognition covers isolated sign classification and continuous signing from video, and is distinct from full sign-language translation.

explainer.example: Given a clip of a single signed word, the system classifies it as one of a fixed set of signs.
